Hi @jsn1993! Thanks for the detailed diagnostic trace and layer-scaling comparison between the 9B and 27B hybrid checkpoints. 

I'm picking this up. I'll inspect `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` to check how the mamba/GDN cache budget and per-sequence draft token slots ($1 + k$) are being accounted for during speculative decode scheduling.

@jsn1993 — to confirm the mechanism I think is behind this, I have added logs to my PR, can you run this and give the logs.

MTP reserves an extra mamba/GDN state block per sequence (num_speculative_blocks = num_speculative_tokens), which inflates each request's state footprint and lowers max_concurrency = num_blocks / num_blocks_per_request. On the 48-GDN-layer 27B the per-request state is already large, so this halving is what drops the effective batch to ~3. The 24-layer 9B has a big enough pool to absorb it. This log confirms or kills that.

Please run it twice with your usual 8×256 repro and paste the [diag55533] lines from each:

Run A — MTP on: your existing config (speculative_config={"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}).
Run B — control, MTP off: identical config but with the speculative_config line removed entirely.
The control run is the key part — it holds everything constant except speculation, so any difference is attributable to MTP alone.

What I am looking for:

mamba_cache_mode — decides which state-size formula is live. If it prints all, my hypothesis is likely wrong (the speculative term is negligible there) and we look elsewhere; none/align keeps it in play.
On the Mamba* group, spec_blocks and per_req_blocks — expect spec_blocks to go 1 (Run A) → 0 (Run B), and per_req_blocks to shrink accordingly. That delta is the MTP inflation, isolated from attention.
max_concurrency — expect A < B. Heads up: this figure is computed at max_model_len (4608), so the absolute value won't literally be ~3 at your 256-token decode lengths — the A-vs-B ratio is the signal, not the raw number.

If the mamba group's per_req_blocks drops and max_concurrency rises when spec is off, that pins the concurrency collapse on the per-request speculative state reservation. Thanks!

@jsn1993 @khushali9 @ArjunPakhan — khushali9's hypothesis matches what I see, so here is an independent check on a different box, offered as corroboration (the #55617 A/B on the affected card is still the decisive run). `MambaSpec.num_speculative_blocks = num_speculative_tokens` for every Mamba layer, and `MambaManager` (align mode) charges `1 + k` blocks per Mamba group for the request's lifetime. With the 48 GDN layers in 3 KV groups, a 256-token request needs 1 attention + 3×(1+k) Mamba blocks — 4 at k=0, 7 at k=1 — and once the pool is short the WAITING loop in `v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` breaks on `allocate_slots` returning `None`. That gives a stable window of `floor((num_gpu_blocks − 1) / 7)` requests (the −1 is the null block), zero preemptions, which is the shape of your trace. Caveat: my 48 GB box does not collapse naturally (932 / 824 blocks at k=0/1, all 8 run, MTP faster); I reproduced your trace by pinning the pool with `num_gpu_blocks_override`.

vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev451+g1970f3ed4`, RTX 6000 Ada, `RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-INT4` (ships an MTP head), `enforce_eager`, `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype=bfloat16`, `max_model_len=4608`, `max_num_seqs=25`, 8 × 256 random-token prompts, greedy, 48 new tokens; concurrency read by instrumenting `Scheduler.schedule`:

| k | `num_gpu_blocks` | predicted `floor((n−1)/(1+3(1+k)))` | scheduled per step |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 22 / 28 | 3 | **3** (`num_scheduled_tokens = {2,2,2}`) |
| 1 | 29 / 35 | 4 | 4 |
| 1 | 36 | 5 | 5 |
| 1 | 43 | 6 | 6 |
| 1 | 57 | 8 | 8 |
| 0 | 24 / 28 | 5 / 6 | 5 / 6 |
| 2 | 24 | 2 | 2 |

If this is what's biting you, your k=1 pool should be somewhere around 22–28 blocks — `num_gpu_blocks` in the startup log, or `per_req_blocks` from #55617 (the "Maximum concurrency" multiplier is computed at `max_model_len`, as khushali9 noted, so compare block counts). On a 24 GB card the k=0 → k=1 shrink is mostly the MTP head (0.88 GiB bf16 on this checkpoint) coming out of the same `gpu_memory_utilization` budget, not block geometry (~11% on my box). A cheap falsifier that needs no MTP: with speculation off, pass `num_gpu_blocks_override=24` to `LLM(...)` — if bs=8 then collapses to a ~5-wide window, the cause is pool size. _AI assistance (Claude) was used for the code tracing; I ran the measurements._

Thanks @Raymondlol — that's a clean independent confirmation, and the floor((num_gpu_blocks − 1) / (1 + G·(1+k))) window (with G = mamba group count) matches the {2,2,2} trace exactly. Adopting that formulation.

Two things your box surfaced that I want to fold in:

Two compounding causes on the 24 GB card, not one. The per-request +k mamba reservation is the block-geometry half; the MTP head weight (~0.88 GiB bf16) coming out of the same gpu_memory_utilization budget is the other half, shrinking num_gpu_blocks itself when spec is on. So a fix that only tightens the +k accounting won't fully recover throughput on a tight pool — the head cost remains. Worth flagging before anyone proposes a one-liner.

Card-specific. Since your 48 GB box only collapses under a pinned pool, the un-pinned numbers have to come from the affected 4090.
So the decisive run is still @jsn1993's on-card A/B with the #55617 diag, because it reports the real mamba_cache_mode (you assumed align — worth confirming it's not none), the real group count G, and the real num_gpu_blocks. If those differ from your box, the /7 arithmetic shifts.

@jsn1993 — when you run it, could you also paste the num_gpu_blocks line from both the k=1 and k=0 (spec-off) runs? That lets us separate how much of the shrink is head-weight vs block geometry, which Raymondlol's analysis depends on.

Your num_gpu_blocks_override falsifier is a nice touch — I'll suggest it as the no-MTP cross-check if the on-card numbers line up.

Thanks @khushali9 and @Raymondlol for the clear mathematical breakdown and independent validation on the RTX 6000 Ada!

The breakdown between the **MTP draft head VRAM footprint (~0.88 GB)** and the **per-request Mamba block reservation $(1 + G \cdot (1 + k))$** makes complete sense for why this hits 24 GB cards so severely.

Standing by for @jsn1993's on-card `[diag55533]` output to confirm `mamba_cache_mode` and exact block metrics!
@jsn1993 any update on the run for my logs.
@jsn1993 Any update with the log. Thanks

Since 2026-08-23 ~22:00 UTC this engine has been running what I described above as the mitigation: stock `intel/vllm:latest` (0.21.1.dev17+g0a475), `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90`, no patched-kernel bind mounts. It ran clean for roughly three days and then degenerated again in exactly the same way: a content canary that sends a fixed short prompt every 20 minutes got a reply consisting only of `!` repeated to the token cap, with `finish_reason` normal. ```
image                     intel/vllm:latest (0.21.1.dev17+g0a475)
--gpu-memory-utilization  0.90
--max-num-seqs            12

model                     Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 (head_dim 256), single card, no TP

## Update — bug also occurs WITHOUT MTP

After filing this issue, we removed `--speculative-config` from our config and retested. The same crash pattern recurred:

- **Config change**: `speculative_config=None` (everything else identical)
- **Time to first crash**: ~14 minutes after engine ready
- **Same stack trace**: `sample_tokens` RPC timeout → `EngineDeadError`
- **Same `step_counter=0`** in scheduler dump

So the bug is **not specific to MTP**. The issue is somewhere deeper in the v0.20.0 V1 engine path on the GLM-5.1 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) + LMCache + TP=8 stack. Disabling MTP and `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` extends MTTF to varying degrees but doesn't fix the underlying hang.

Reproduction is otherwise identical to the original report; just remove the `--speculative-config` flag and the bug still fires.

This makes the underlying root cause likely:
- The DSA path itself (without MTP being involved)
- Or the LMCache `LMCacheConnectorV1` integration with v0.20.0's V1 engine `step_with_batch_queue`
- Or a v0.20.0 specific change to the scheduler / async pipeline that doesn't tolerate this connector setup

Please consider this a v0.20.0 GLM-5.1 + LMCache regression, not a pure MTP bug.

## Additional Data: v0.20.0 MP Mode Crash + DeepEP Root Cause Analysis

### New Crash (April 28)

Reproduced on rtp-14 (8x H200 bare metal, NVLink) running v0.20.0 with LMCache MP mode (single-container pattern). Same `sample_tokens timed out` after ~7 min of serving.

**Pre-crash state:**
```
22:29:34 - Avg prompt throughput: 5924.3 tokens/s, Running: 3 reqs, GPU KV cache: 37.1%
22:29:44 - Avg prompt throughput: 2257.5 tokens/s, Running: 3 reqs, GPU KV cache: 37.1%
22:29:54 - Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s,    Running: 3 reqs, GPU KV cache: 37.1%
22:34:36 - TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out.
```

Progressive stall: throughput drops 5924 → 2257 → 0.0 over 20s while 3 requests stay "running". No CUDA error, no OOM, no worker death. GPUs at 100% util (stuck, not idle). KV cache at 37% — no memory pressure.

### Code Path Analysis

Traced the hang through the source:

1. `sample_tokens` is not the hang site — it's a downstream timeout. The actual hang is in `execute_model` during the model forward pass.

2. With `LMCacheConnectorV1`/`LMCacheMPConnector` active, `kv_output_aggregator is not None`, so `output_rank = None` (line 350 of `multiproc_executor.py`). This means **all 8 workers must respond** — if any single worker hangs in `execute_model`, the executor blocks on `mq.dequeue(timeout=300)` waiting for that worker.

3. The progressive throughput drop (5924 → 2257 → 0.0) suggests one worker fell behind, then the collective operations stalled all workers.

### Most Likely Root Cause: DeepEP NVLink All-to-All

GLM-5.1-FP8 with `--enable-expert-parallel` uses DeepEP for MoE dispatch/combine. Each MoE layer does:
- `dispatch()` — NVLink SM-copy all-to-all (async)
- Expert GEMM
- `combine()` — NVLink SM-copy all-to-all (waits for dispatch)

DeepEP's intra-node kernels operate directly on GPU shared memory via NVLink. Unlike NCCL (which has timeout and error reporting), **DeepEP has no timeout detection**. If one GPU stalls (memory pressure, ECC error, NVLink congestion, unbalanced expert routing), the other GPUs' SM-copy kernels spin waiting for data — showing 100% GPU utilization with no forward progress and no error.

This matches all symptoms:
- 100% GPU util (spinning in NVLink SM-copy kernel)
- No CUDA error (DeepEP doesn't report them)
- No OOM (37% KV cache)
- Stochastic trigger after 7-38 min (depends on specific token routing patterns)
- Progressive stall (one worker falls behind → collective blocks all)

### Proposed Diagnostic

**Test without expert-parallel:**
```
# Remove --enable-expert-parallel, keep everything else identical
--tensor-parallel-size 8
# (no --enable-expert-parallel)
```
If the hang disappears, it confirms DeepEP as the root cause.

**py-spy dump at hang time:**
```bash
py-spy dump --pid $(pgrep -f VllmWorker-0) --nonblocking
```
Expected to show all workers stuck in:
```
deepep_ht.py _finalize() → deep_ep.buffer.combine() → <C extension blocked>
```

**NCCL debug:**
```
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL
```
To differentiate NCCL deadlock from DeepEP deadlock.

### Environment
- vLLM v0.20.0 (self-built `v0.20.0-cu130-local`)
- PyTorch 2.11, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer (bundled)
- GLM-5.1-FP8, TP=8, EP, FP8 KV cache, MLA
- `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`
- `--disable-custom-all-reduce`
- LMCache v0.4.4+nw.mp (MP mode, single-container)
- 8x H200 via NVLink, bare metal

## Root Cause Found: FutureWrapper Refactoring in multiproc_executor.py

### Key finding: `shm_broadcast.py` is identical between v0.19.1 and v0.20.0

```
md5sum: 6715dbec1b803812fe7b42c1ca993ddc (both versions)
```

The hang manifests in `shm_broadcast.py`'s `acquire_read` / `_spin_condition.wait()`, but the bug is in the **caller** — `multiproc_executor.py`'s `collective_rpc()` was refactored between v0.19.1 and v0.20.0.

### What changed

**v0.19.1 (working):**
```python
if non_block:
    future = FutureWrapper(self.futures_queue, aggregate=aggregate)
    self.futures_queue.appendleft((future, get_response))
    return future
# Synchronous path: drain pending futures FIRST, then call get_response directly
while self.futures_queue:
    future, get_fut_response = self.futures_queue.pop()
    future.wait_for_response(get_fut_response)
return aggregate(get_response())
```

**v0.20.0 (broken):**
```python
future = FutureWrapper(self.futures_queue, get_response=get_response, aggregate=aggregate)
return future if non_block else future.result()
```

In v0.20.0, **every call** (even synchronous) creates a `FutureWrapper` that captures `get_response` as an instance attribute. The `get_response` closure captures `deadline` at enqueue time. When the future is eventually resolved (after draining the LIFO queue), the deadline may have already expired.

### The infinite hang path

1. `execute_model` dispatched `non_block=True` → FutureWrapper A created with deadline T₁
2. `sample_tokens` dispatched `non_block=True` → FutureWrapper B created with deadline T₂
3. Worker stalls briefly during `execute_model` (FlashInfer 0.6.7 autotuning, Triton JIT, CUDA graph capture — any variable-time GPU operation)
4. When `.result()` drains the queue, FutureWrapper A's `get_response()` runs with deadline T₁ that has already passed
5. `dequeue_timeout = deadline - time.monotonic()` computes a **negative value**
6. Negative timeout flows to `poller.poll()` — **zmq interprets negative timeout as poll forever**
7. Worker hangs indefinitely in `_spin_condition.wait()`
8. After 300s, the outer timeout fires: `TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`

### Why LMCache amplifies it

With `kv_output_aggregator` present (LMCache active), `output_rank = None`, forcing all 8 worker MQs to be drained sequentially. If any single worker's dequeue hits the negative-timeout path, the entire `get_response()` blocks. Without LMCache, only rank 0 responds — 8× less chance of hitting the race.

### Why DeepEP amplifies it further

DeepEP V1's NVLink SM-copy kernels have highly variable latency (no timeout, no error detection). A single slow dispatch/combine operation can stall a worker long enough to push the closure's captured deadline into the past. NCCL's `allgather_reducescatter` has lower variance, explaining the 5-10× MTTF improvement we observed (7-38 min with DeepEP → ~2hr with NCCL EP).

### Why FlashInfer autotuning amplifies it

FlashInfer 0.6.7 (shipped in v0.20.0) introduces new Triton autotuning paths that can cause 10-30s stalls on first execution. This pushes the async future pipeline into the degenerate case. We previously observed `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` improving MTTF 8× on DeepEP.

### Proposed fix

**Minimal (one-liner):** In `get_response()`, clamp timeout to non-negative:
```python
dequeue_timeout = None if deadline is None else max(0, deadline - time.monotonic())
```

**Belt-and-suspenders:** Also guard in `SpinCondition.wait()`:
```python
if timeout_ms is not None and timeout_ms < 0:
    return  # already expired, don't block
```

**Architectural (cleanest):** Revert the FutureWrapper change so synchronous calls bypass the queue entirely (as v0.19.1 did), eliminating the closure-captured-deadline staleness window.

### Evidence

| Configuration | MTTF | Explanation |
|---|---|---|
| v0.19.1 + DeepEP | Stable (days) | No FutureWrapper refactoring, deadline is fresh |
| v0.20.0 + DeepEP | 7-38 min | Stale deadline + high-variance DeepEP + FlashInfer autotune |
| v0.20.0 + NCCL EP | ~2 hrs | Stale deadline + lower-variance NCCL, fewer autotune triggers |
| v0.20.0 + DeepEP + `--no-flashinfer-autotune` | ~5 hrs | Removes one source of worker stall |

All configurations crash on v0.20.0; none crash on v0.19.1. The common denominator is the FutureWrapper refactoring.

### Environment
- vLLM v0.20.0, PyTorch 2.11, CUDA 13.0
- GLM-5.1-FP8, TP=8, expert-parallel, FP8 KV cache, MLA
- 8x H200 (NVLink) and 8x B200 (NVLink), bare metal

### Source-dive findings (vLLM SHA `d4004455d`)

Per `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`:

- **Lines 291-298**: a shared workspace `decode_seq_lens_buffer` is allocated as a flat contiguous 1D `int32` tensor. The comment explicitly says "Native MTP views this as `(B, max_decode_len)` at runtime, keeping context_lens contiguous even when max_decode_len is smaller than next_n."
- **Lines 451-464** (MTP native path, `use_native and next_n > 1`): a prefix slice + `.view(num_decodes, max_decode_len)` is taken from that buffer. A prefix slice + view of a contiguous 1D buffer **should** yield a contiguous 2D tensor.
- The flatten path at lines 376-441 also explicitly returns `self.decode_seq_lens_buffer[:num_decode_tokens]` — a contiguous prefix slice.

So by static reading, `seq_lens` SHOULD already be contiguous when it reaches the asserting kernel at line 613. But the C-kernel assertion at `csrc/apis/attention.hpp:201` fires in practice at K>1.

### Hypotheses (we haven't verified)

Some path we haven't traced lets a non-contiguous tensor reach the kernel. Candidates:

1. The `compress_ratio > 1` branch at `indexer.py:589-603` (DeepSeek-V4 path)
2. A drafting-only construction at the caller (`llm_base_proposer.py:817`) that bypasses the shared workspace
3. A subtle CUDA-graph capture/replay quirk where stride information differs between capture and replay
4. `seq_lens.unsqueeze(1)` interacting unexpectedly with the in-place assignment to `seq_lens_buffer` when `next_n > 1`

### Suggested defensive patch (always-safe two-layer guard)

Even if the root cause is upstream of the assertion site, adding `.contiguous()` at the call boundary fixes the symptom for users today and has zero overhead in the common case (`.contiguous()` on an already-contiguous tensor returns `self`):

```python
# vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py:613 — narrow fix for GLM-DSA + MTP
self.scheduler_metadata_buffer[:] = get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(
    seq_lens.contiguous(), block_size, num_sms,  # +.contiguous()
)
```

```python
# vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py:404 — defense in depth at the wrapper
def get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(context_lens, block_size, num_sms):
    return _get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata_impl(
        context_lens.contiguous(), block_size, num_sms  # +.contiguous()
    )
```

Two layers because:
- The narrow fix catches the specific GLM-DSA / DeepSeek code path
- The wrapper catches anyone else who calls `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata` with a non-contiguous tensor (future-proof)

Stay on `num_speculative_tokens=1`. K=1 still gives meaningful TTFT improvements as documented (we observe -50 to -72% TTFT across c=1..c=64 + ~33% MTP acceptance). We're hitting what looks like the same deadlock on a **different model and TP size**, and traced it to **async scheduling being auto-enabled for MTP**. Sharing a reproduction and root-cause analysis in case it helps move this forward.

## Environment
- vLLM **0.23.0** (official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.23.0` image)
- Model: **Qwen3-Next 27B** with the `qwen3_next_mtp` MTP head (hybrid linear-attention / Mamba + MoE)
- **TP=2** on 2×A800-80GB
- Serving flags (abridged): `--speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_next_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 262144`
- **We did NOT pass `--async-scheduling`.**

## Symptom (matches this issue)
Under sustained production traffic, generation silently stalls: `Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s` while `Running: N>0, Waiting: M>0`, **GPU utilization 0% at idle power**, no exception, no NCCL timeout, no self-recovery; `/metrics` keeps returning 200.

`py-spy dump` at the moment of hang (TP=2):
- **EngineCore** main thread: `run_busy_loop → _process_engine_step → step_with_batch_queue (v1/engine/core.py) → MultiprocExecutor.execute_model → collective_rpc` — i.e. blocked handing off the next command on `rpc_broadcast_mq` (the `enqueue`/`acquire_write` side, which is called with `timeout=None`).
- **Both workers**: `worker_busy_loop → shm_broadcast.dequeue → acquire_read → SpinCondition.wait` — **the exact stack reported in this issue**.

So the engine is spinning trying to enqueue the next command onto the broadcast MQ while both workers idle-wait for a command to read — a broadcast ring-buffer standstill on `rpc_broadcast_mq`. CPU is burning (spin-poll), which is why there is no NCCL timeout and GPU sits at 0%.

## Root cause we found: async scheduling is auto-enabled for MTP
The user never asked for async scheduling. In `VllmConfig.__post_init__` (`vllm/config/vllm.py`), when `scheduler_config.async_scheduling is None` it is **auto-enabled** unless an incompatibility matches. The spec-decode guard only disables async when the method is *not* in `EagleModelTypes`:

```python
elif (self.speculative_config is not None
      and self.speculative_config.method not in get_args(EagleModelTypes)
      and self.speculative_config.method not in get_args(NgramGPUTypes)):
    self.scheduler_config.async_scheduling = False
```

But in `vllm/config/speculative.py`, `EagleModelTypes` **includes** `MTPModelTypes`:

```python
EagleModelTypes = Literal["eagle", "eagle3", "extract_hidden_states", MTPModelTypes, DFlashModelTypes]
```

so `"mtp"` and `"qwen3_next_mtp"` are in `get_args(EagleModelTypes)` → the disable branch is skipped → async is auto-enabled. Confirmed in the logs:

```
[config/vllm.py:999] Asynchronous scheduling is enabled.
```

This is what silently puts every MTP deployment on the `step_with_batch_queue` (batch_queue) pipelined path — the path where this hang lives. **Both 0.23.0 and current `main` still do this** (the resolver is unchanged aside from a ROCm-only branch).

## Why the pipelined path is fragile here
`step_with_batch_queue` issues `execute_model` / `sample_tokens` via `collective_rpc(non_block=True)` and reads results lazily (it returns early while `len(batch_queue) < batch_queue_size` and there are still requests). With **structured output + MTP**, sampling is deferred (`scheduler_output.pending_structured_output_tokens` → `deferred_scheduler_output`), and the extra `sample_tokens` RPC for that step is appended a step later — so the number and timing of commands enqueued onto `rpc_broadcast_mq` becomes irregular. Under KV saturation (in our load harness we sit at **~99% GPU KV cache usage with ~120 `Deferred` reqs**), the writer/reader positions on the fixed broadcast ring appear to desync, and because the command-side `enqueue → acquire_write` is called with `timeout=None`, the engine spins forever. Note `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` does **not** help — it only bounds the response-side `dequeue`, not the command-side `enqueue`.

Root-cause: `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` — the unconditional `break` at line 781 prevents `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` promotions when a plain `WAITING` request blocks allocation.

**Deadlock sequence:**

1. Req B1 matches CPU cache, `allocate_slots` succeeds, status → `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`, consuming ~1 249 of 2 048 GPU blocks.
2. Req A1 also has a CPU hit. `_inflight_prefill_reserved_blocks()` now includes B1's reserved blocks. With `scheduler_reserve_full_isl=True` (default), A1's full sequence (~1 600 blocks) cannot fit — `allocate_slots` returns `None`. A1 stays `WAITING`.
3. Every step: FCFS places A1 before B1 in `skipped_waiting`. A1 is plain `WAITING`, so the blocked-status promotion check is skipped; `allocate_slots` fails again → `break` at line 781. B1 is never dequeued; `_try_promote_blocked_waiting_request` is never called.

B1's CPU→GPU transfer completes (`finished_recving_kv_req_ids` is populated) but B1 is never promoted. Engine stalls at `scheduled=0` indefinitely.

**Fix region (line 781):** when the failing entry is plain `WAITING`, continue scanning for `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` promotions instead of breaking immediately.

`self.method == "mtp"` is at `:1008`, so your predicate applies unchanged. Since this is Python-level ordering rather than a kernel, the sm75-to-sm121 gap offers no protection, which is part of why your result reads as relevant to me despite the hardware distance.

**Why my instrumentation missed it.** I have been running device-side probes for several weeks: block-index bounds, accepted-count range, pointer identity across graph replays, and geometry at the align copy boundary. The most recent 99-hour run reported 30 million in-range state indices, 8 million in-range accepted-count values, and **9.9 million graph replays with zero pointer mismatches**. On your mechanism, stable pointers are the premise rather than evidence against it, and every one of those probes measures addresses or ranges rather than buffer contents. They are structurally blind to it. That is worth saying plainly, because a clean probe pane looks like exoneration and is not.

**Yes to the focused patch**, please. I would run it on the same image the control is running now, as its own single-variable layer, and report the result either way. If it holds here it would be both a diagnosis and a usable mitigation, since it respects the constraints I care about: MTP, prefix caching, target CUDA graphs and the CUTLASS MoE backend all stay on. Your reported 50-75 tok/s is also encouraging next to the roughly 30% per-stream cost I pay for launch blocking.

One question, if you have the data. When you retired each MTP forward, did you ever try narrowing further, to a synchronization only before the persistent-input write rather than after every `self.model(...)`? I ask because it would separate "the previous forward must complete" from "the device must be quiet", and the first is the claim your explanation actually needs.

**Field report: sm86, k=2, vLLM 0.28.0 — 21 h unmasked, no IMA. Bounded negative, not a clean bill.**

Same rig class as the OP (single RTX 3090, syv-ai/HyperQwen — formerly qwen38-27b-rtx3090 — patch series, fp8 KV, FlashInfer forced, MTP, prefix caching + chunked prefill). Posting because every data point in this thread is 0.27.1 or 0.26.0, and because nobody has an sm86 k=2 arm.

**Config**

```
GPU            RTX 3090 (sm86), driver 595.84
vLLM           0.28.0  (torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0)
HyperQwen      231592a, 36-patch series
model          Qwen3.8-27B W4A16-AutoRound ("-fast" variant)
spec           method=mtp, num_spec_tokens=2, draft_sample_method=probabilistic
attention      FlashInferBackend (forced: FLASH_ATTN and TRITON_ATTN both refuse fp8 KV on sm86)
kv cache       fp8 (e4m3), --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16
cudagraph      PIECEWISE
scheduling     --async-scheduling ON
ctx            --max-model-len 150000, --max-num-seqs 8, --max-num-batched-tokens 2048
gpu-util       0.97   (KV pool 201,295 tok, 1.34x concurrency at 150k)
env            VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0
               CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING is NOT set  <- unmasked arm
```

**Result — 21 h 10 m continuous, single process, no restarts**

```
AcceleratorError / illegal memory access in serve log : 0
Xid entries (journalctl -k, since process start)      : 0
NVRM / nvidia errors                                  : 0

requests finished           : ~925  (922 stop, 3 length)
drafts                      : ~112,000
draft tokens                : ~224,000
accepted draft tokens       : ~178,000   (79.5% acceptance)
preemptions                 : 1
max prompt_tokens observed  : 125,460
```

**Exposure in the reported fault window.** meowsigma reports faults at `num_computed_tokens` ≈ 23.6K–26.2K; liuhaibin0528 (HyperQwen #34) at 28,863 and 34,111. Of the finished requests in this window, **11.6% had prompt_tokens in 23k–35k**, and none faulted. Generation length distribution: median 120, p90 417, p99 ~6,000, max 8,192 — so this is a long-prompt/short-output shape, not a long-decode shape. Traffic is real application load, not synthetic benchmarking.

**What this is worth, honestly.** 21 h is roughly half liuhaibin0528's ~40 h inter-fault interval and a fifth of swesty's window, and per-request decode here is short. Against a fault with two observations in 80 h, this is a bounded negative, not evidence of absence. Taking mhenrichsen's framing from the sibling thread: absence over a fraction of the inter-crash interval is not a clean bill. I'll re-post if it faults, and again at a longer horizon if it does not.

**On erdholion's soak request.** You asked for an arm on a #50729-containing build. This is not that — #50729 is absent from 0.28.0, and it is not in the HyperQwen patch series either (checked all 36 patches). So this arm does not test the copy race. What it does establish: **0.28.0 alone neither fixes nor visibly worsens this class on sm86**, and the fault does not reproduce readily at k=2 on this hardware within 21 h.

**On k.** meowsigma reported k∈{1,2} vs k=3 as small-sample noise on his sm86 box. erdholion's k=2 point is sm120 and it crashed. This is the first sm86 k=2 arm I can find in either thread, and it is clean so far — which I read as "k=2 is not obviously protective," consistent with meowsigma, rather than as a mitigation.

**Two config deltas from the OP that may or may not matter**, flagged because they are the only things I can see that differ:

1. **Driver 595.84** vs the OP's 595.71.05.
2. `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` — FlashInfer is still the attention backend, but its sampler is off. Given the fault surfaces in flashinfer `build()` paths, someone may want to rule this in or out; I did not set it as a mitigation and have not A/B'd it.

A single-variable backend A/B is not available on this hardware: on sm86 with fp8 KV, FLASH_ATTN refuses ("requires FA3 on SM90") and TRITON_ATTN refuses ("native FP8 (fp8e4nv) requires SM89+"), so FlashInfer is the only backend. The escape is `--attention-backend=TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype=int8_per_token_head`, which is a two-variable change and costs ~25% wall (and −44% prefill at 60K on this checkpoint), so I have not taken it.

If a specific arm would be useful, I can likely run it — this is a stable long-running deployment on real traffic, so I can hold a config and report back.

54371.title: [Qwen4Exp] Support UVA PLE-offload and Engram tensor parallelism
54371.body:
## Purpose Add UVA-based PLE offload and Engram tensor parallelism (ETP) for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. `--engram-config` controls PLE weight storage and embedding sharding: - `cpu_offload=true` stores each local PLE weight shard in pinned CPU memory. The GPU reads the required rows directly through CUDA Unified Virtual Addressing (UVA), using a dedicated CUDA stream. Offload can also be enabled with `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1` when `cpu_offload` is omitted; an explicit `cpu_offload` value takes precedence. - `cpu_offload=false` keeps PLE weights on the GPU. - `embedding_across_dp=false` uses `ETP=TP`, keeping a separate TP-sharded PLE table in each DP replica. - `embedding_across_dp=true` uses `ETP=TP×DP`, sharding the PLE table across all DP replicas. Offload and cross-DP sharding can be enabled independently. Both options default to false. ## Design The PLE embedding implementation is organized into three abstraction levels: ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Level1["Level 1 — N-gram embedding semantics"] NGram["Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding
computes request-dependent n-gram IDs
and orchestrates forward/prefetch"] end subgraph Level2["Level 2 — device-specific storage and execution"] Device["Qwen4ExpPLEDeviceEmbedding
GPU-resident weights
resident forward path
prefetch is a no-op"] Pinned["Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding
pinned CPU weights
UVA lookup on a side stream
prefetch and finalization"] end subgraph Level3["Level 3 — common embedding and weight-format foundation"] Base["Qwen4ExpPLEEmbedding
common backend interface
ETP sharding, DP ID gathering
and local-row selection"] Method["Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod
weight creation, lookup format
and dequantization interface"] BF16["Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod
BF16 embedding"] FP8["Qwen4ExpPLEFp8EmbeddingMethod
FP8 embedding and global scale"] end NGram -->|"owns one backend selected at initialization"| Device NGram -->|"owns one backend selected at initialization"| Pinned Device -.->|"inherits"| Base Pinned -.->|"inherits"| Base Base -->|"delegates weight-format behavior"| Method Method --> BF16 Method --> FP8 ``` - `Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding` contains the model-specific n-gram computation and coordinates `start_prefetch()` and `forward()`. - `Qwen4ExpPLEDeviceEmbedding` and `Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding` encapsulate device-specific allocation and execution. The pinned-host backend implements the asynchronous UVA path, while the device backend retains the resident lookup path. - `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbedding` provides the shared embedding contract and ETP logic. It delegates weight-format-specific creation and dequantization to `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod`, with separate BF16 and FP8 implementations. ## Not a duplicate Searched the open PRs for [Qwen4Exp PLE offload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+Qwen4Exp+PLE+offload), and [PLE UVA](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+PLE+UVA). There are related PRs, but they use materially different designs: - [#53899](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53899) uses a dedicated CPU offload worker and transfers selected rows back to GPU workers. This PR keeps the table in process-local pinned memory and lets the GPU read the required rows directly through UVA, without an offload worker or IPC row transfer. - [#54129](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129) uses disk-backed mmap storage to reduce host-memory residency. This PR intentionally keeps the complete local shard pinned in RAM for direct UVA access. - [#54431](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54431) optimizes ragged n-gram ID generation for the worker-based offload path. - [#54517](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54517) fuses the PLE compute kernels and is orthogonal to the pinned-table storage, asynchronous UVA lookup, and NP topology introduced here. ## Test Plan ```bash python -m pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py python -m pytest -q tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -k engram python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py -k engram git diff --check ``` ## End-to-end validation: Run Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with TP4, DP2, and MTP3 for all four `--engram-config` combinations: | `cpu_offload` | `embedding_across_dp` | Expected PLE storage | Expected ETP topology | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | false | false | GPU memory | ETP4, a separate TP-sharded table per DP replica | | false | true | GPU memory | ETP8, one table sharded across both DP replicas | | true | false | Pinned CPU memory | ETP4, a separate TP-sharded table per DP replica | | true | true | Pinned CPU memory | ETP8, one table sharded across both DP replicas | For each combination, verify storage and topology against the table, exercise CUDA Graph capture and replay with uneven DP loads (including an idle replica), and run GSM8K. ## Test Result - Added and updated PLE, Engram configuration, and CLI tests: 50 passed. - Ruff checks on the PLE, Engram configuration, and communicator files: passed. - `git diff --check`: passed. - BF16 TP2/DP1/MTP3 startup and serving with `cpu_offload=true` and `embedding_across_dp=false`: passed. - Both TP ranks reported BF16 PLE weights on CPU with pinned storage enabled. - GSM8K: `0.9727` mean accuracy over 1,319 samples. ## Performance Results Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`. Prefill uses 8K input at concurrency 2; decode uses 1024 output tokens at concurrency 64 with MTP=3. The workloads use synthetic random-token inputs. The `cpu_offload` and `embedding_across_dp` columns correspond to fields in `--engram-config`. | `cpu_offload` | `embedding_across_dp` | Parallel Configuration | Prefill tok/s | Raw Decode tok/s | Draft Acceptance | Seq-steps/s | Est. C64 Step (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | false | false | TP4/DP1 | 33544.13 | 2261.37 | 53.72% | 865.89 | 73.91 | | true | false | TP4/DP1 | 33322.61 | 2245.84 | 51.56% | 881.83 | 72.58 | | false | false | DP2/TP4/EP8/FI2S | 26872.32 | 2762.68 | 39.80% | 1259.20 | 50.83 | | false | true | DP2/TP4/EP8/FI2S | 26763.57 | 2775.67 | 43.28% | 1207.65 | 53.00 | | true | false | DP2/TP4/EP8/FI2S | 25751.63 | 3101.35 | 46.48% | 1295.25 | 49.41 | Notes: - `Prefill tok/s` is total token throughput. `Raw Decode tok/s` is output-token throughput and is affected by MTP acceptance. - For MTP=3: `Seq-steps/s = Raw Decode tok/s / (1 + 3 × Draft Acceptance)`. - `Est. C64 Step = 64 / Seq-steps/s × 1000`. - `FI2S` means FlashInfer NVLink Two-Sided, the EP MoE All-to-All backend. - After acceptance normalization, the offload decode differences are +1.84% for TP4 and +2.86% for DP2; these single-run differences should be treated as approximately flat. > AI assistance was used for code analysis, implementation, refactoring, and test drafting. 54722.title: [Qwen4] validate FP8 PLE weight scale after loading
54722.body:
## Purpose

Fix a fail-open risk in the Qwen3.8 Flash Next FP8 PLE weight loading path.

If `ngram_embedding.weight_scale` is missing or incorrectly mapped, the registered parameter could remain uninitialized without being detected. This PR:

- Stores the BF16 PLE global scale as FP32 so the existing sentinel initialization applies.
- Validates the sentinel in `process_weights_after_loading()` after all checkpoint shards have been processed.

Thanks to @Dev-Jahn for identifying and reporting this issue.

## Not a duplicate

Searched the open PRs for [Qwen3.8 PLE weight_scale](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+Qwen3.8+PLE+weight_scale) and [FP8 PLE scale](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+FP8+PLE+scale). I did not find an open PR addressing this missing post-load validation.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ple_layer.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py

git diff --check
```

## Test Result
* Unit tests: 11 passed.
* Pre-commit hooks: all passed.
* git diff --check: passed.
* Missing scale now raises ValueError during post-load processing.
